name: open-pencil
works_with: Claude Code, Cursor, Windsurf, Codex and other skills hosts
short: Teaches your coding agent to open, inspect, edit and export Figma .fig files with the OpenPencil CLI and MCP server.
what: OpenPencil is an open source design editor that reads and writes Figma `.fig` files. This skill teaches your agent its CLI and MCP server, in two modes: headless on a `.fig` file, or live on the document open in the editor. The agent can print the node tree, query nodes with XPath, pull design tokens, lint for accessibility, run Figma Plugin API scripts and export to PNG, SVG, PDF or JSX.
who: Designers and front-end developers who want an agent to work with Figma files without Figma. The project says it is in active development with some rough edges.
needs: npm or Bun, for the CLI and MCP server
Optional: the OpenPencil desktop app, for app mode

steps.title: Optional: add the MCP server
steps.text: Set `OPENPENCIL_MCP_ROOT` to limit file access to one folder. It defaults to the current folder.
steps.code:
npm install -g @open-pencil/mcp
claude mcp add --scope user open-pencil -- openpencil-mcp

steps.title: Optional: install the editor
steps.text: On macOS with Homebrew. Or download it from the releases page, or use the web app at app.openpencil.dev.

try.label: From the README
try.where: Your terminal or your coding agent
try.text: Find small frames and export one at 2x: `openpencil query design.fig "//FRAME[@width < 300]"`, then `openpencil export design.fig --node 1:23 -s 2 -o button@2x.png`.

watch: `eval` with `-w` runs JavaScript against your file and writes the result back. Keep a copy of the original.
Official app builds send one anonymous ping a day and share usage stats only if you agree. The privacy page lists every field and how to turn it off.
The desktop app starts a local MCP server on 127.0.0.1 ports 7600 and 7601 when `@open-pencil/mcp` is installed globally.
The built-in AI chat uses your own API key for the provider you pick.
